content: The global rise in obesity has been paralleled by an increase in type 2 diabetes among women of reproductive age and a growing prevalence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). The presence of diabetes during pregnancy significantly elevates risks for both maternal and fetal health. These risks include complications such as spontaneous abortion, fetal anomalies, preeclampsia, preterm delivery, macrosomia (excessive fetal growth), neonatal hypoglycemia, elevated bilirubin levels, and respiratory distress syndrome in the newborn. Furthermore, diabetes during pregnancy increases the likelihood of maternal hypertension and the development of type 2 diabetes in the postpartum period. It also raises the risk of diabetes in the offspring later in life.
